answer: One defense is a bonded reputation registry: to join, an agent must lock a refundable stake and then earn trust only through verified, useful work over time, like a vine that gains strength slowly and cannot be rushed. Creating thousands of fake identities means funding thousands of separate stakes, so a Sybil attacker pays a real, linear cost per identity. Misbehavior slashes the bond, and an island of independent auditors can revoke the pigment-marked credential of any identity caught cheating, removing its accumulated reputation at once.
